name: Duolingo AI Ethics Policy & Integrity Stance
summary: Duolingo published its first Responsible AI Standards for the Duolingo English Test (DET) in April 2023, with subsequent updates in 2024 and 2025. Duolingo's business model underwent a major shift in 2023 when it replaced human content contractors with AI (raising ethics concerns about labor). For the DET specifically, Duolingo deployed a sophisticated human-in-the-loop AI proctoring and cheating detection system, including LLM-assisted cheating detection research. Duolingo's integrity approach is notable for its combination of AI detection tools WITH human expert review — not AI alone.
ai_use_policy: Duolingo's learning platform: AI is deeply integrated into instruction (personalized lessons, hint generation, conversation practice). AI use is the product itself — Duolingo does not restrict AI use in learning. DET exam context: strict prohibitions on AI assistance during the test. The test uses webcam proctoring, behavior analysis, and AI comparison against historical responses to detect cheating.
academic_fraud_definition: For the DET: cheating includes using AI tools during the exam to generate written or spoken responses; using scripts, notes, or assistance from other people; sharing test content. Duolingo distinguishes between AI-assisted cheating (using AI during the test) and AI-supported learning (using Duolingo's own AI features to prepare).
detection_mechanisms: Four-layer detection: (1) AI/ML algorithms monitoring test-taker behavior for unusual patterns; (2) Proctoring software with webcam recording and screen monitoring; (3) AI comparing writing responses to internet content databases and historical test sessions; (4) Human-in-the-loop expert reviewers evaluating flagged sessions. 2024 paper: 'Detecting LLM-Assisted Cheating on Open-Ended Writing Tasks on Language Proficiency Tests' — presented at EMNLP 2024.
penalties: Test score cancellation. Permanent ban from Duolingo English Test for serious violations. Reporting to universities that accepted the DET score.
transparency_requirements: Duolingo publishes Responsible AI Standards as a public document (updated annually). Methodology for cheating detection published in academic papers. This level of transparency is notable — most testing organizations do not publish detailed detection methods.
vietnamese_law_reference: [uncertain] — DET is used by Vietnamese students applying to international universities. No specific Vietnamese law reference.
documented_vn_cases: [uncertain] — No specific Vietnam cases documented in available sources.
vn_university_responses: DET is accepted by 5,000+ programs globally including some in Vietnam. Vietnamese students take DET as an IELTS/TOEFL alternative. The integrity standards apply regardless of test location.
ai_tutor_vs_cheater_framing: Duolingo's framing is nuanced: AI IS the product/tutor in their learning platform; AI is the cheater-enabler in their exam context. The company navigates this tension by strictly separating learning (AI-enabled) from testing (AI-prohibited). This dual stance is a practical model for EdTech researchers: AI integration in learning ≠ AI permission in assessment.
responsible_ai_definition: Duolingo's four standards: (1) Validity and Reliability — test is suitable for purpose; (2) Fairness — democratization, accessibility, inclusion; (3) Privacy and Security — secure administration, privacy protection, cheating prevention; (4) Accountability and Transparency — documentation and dissemination of AI use. Notably, their responsible AI definition is test-centered, not generically about student AI use.
key_researchers: Duolingo Research team — published at EMNLP 2024 on LLM cheating detection. Human-in-the-loop AI proctoring paper (arxiv.org/html/2403.14711v1 — 'Human-in-the-Loop AI for Cheating Ring Detection').
company_ethics_policy: Full policy: 'The Duolingo English Test Responsible AI Standards' — publicly available at duolingo-papers.s3.amazonaws.com. Updated versions published annually. The standards include stakeholder consultation requirements and bias testing requirements for AI models used in testing.
framework_name: Duolingo English Test Responsible AI Standards
framework_principles: Validity and Reliability, Fairness, Privacy and Security, Accountability and Transparency. Each standard has goals and subgoals geared toward implementation. Human-in-the-loop is a core architectural principle — AI flags, humans decide on high-stakes determinations.
implementation_challenges: The cheating arms race: as AI detection improves, AI cheating tools also improve. 'Can AI detect AI?' blog post (Duolingo, 2024) acknowledges the detection challenge. LLM-assisted writing is difficult to distinguish from strong human writing with certainty. Duolingo chose a probabilistic approach combined with human review rather than binary AI detection.
student_perspective: Students attempt to cheat on DET due to high stakes (immigration, university admission). Cheating rings have been documented (human helpers physically assisting test takers). AI cheating adds a new vector. From Vietnamese student perspective: DET is popular partly because it is accessible online — this also makes it a target for cheating.
teacher_perspective: Not directly applicable — DET is a standardized test, not classroom assessment. However, Duolingo's model (AI detection + human review) is increasingly cited as a best practice for other EdTech platforms.
recommendations: For EdTech researchers: Duolingo's dual framing (AI as learning tool vs. AI as exam integrity threat) is the most practically sophisticated model available. Recommend adopting Duolingo's four-standard framework (Validity, Fairness, Privacy, Accountability) as a template for AI integrity policies in other EdTech contexts. Human-in-the-loop principle should be a core design requirement — no fully automated AI fraud determination without human review.
